## 2026-11-03 - net-agent (Claude): 1.L15b server + proto half (requester learns its helper's PeerId)

- **Branch/commits:** `feat/1.L15b-helper-peer` (this commit). Not merged.
- **Asked:** a signed endpoint so a job's requester can list its live leases with the helper's PeerId; proto types;
  document that endpoint and the `/nc/blob/1.0.0` direct-chunk framing used by nc-agent `peer.rs`.
- **Done:** `GET /v1/jobs/{id}/leases` (server `peer.rs`, NC-REQ-V1 signed, empty body) returns `JobLeasesResponse`
  (`job_id`, up to 16 `JobLease {lease_id, attempt_id, helper_peer_id, expires_at}`): only `active` leases with
  `expires_at > now`; `helper_peer_id` only while the helper is registered and `peer_seen_at` is within 600 s (same
  `fresh_since` as lease hints), key omitted otherwise. Non-requester device, unknown or malformed job id: the same
  404. New proto messages `JobLease`, `JobLeasesResponse` (new messages only, nothing renumbered); nc-protocol
  `build.rs` adds their serde derive and skip-default on `helper_peer_id`. No migration. proto/README.md documents
  the endpoint and `/nc/blob/1.0.0` (44-byte request, status 0..3, 256 KiB per reply, 10 s request read, 30 s chunk
  and 10 s connect client timeouts, `n + 256` budget charge).
- **Decisions:** device-level ownership (job.requester = caller device), stricter than account. No rate limiter:
  the coordinator has none on any endpoint; signature, nonce and skew window apply, and the response is capped.
- **Verified (real results):** server `cargo fmt --check` ok, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` ok,
  `cargo test` all passed (validation 9 incl. new unsigned GET checks). core nc-protocol fmt/clippy/test ok.
  `infra/verify.ps1`: first run failed in `docker compose build` (buildkit "parent snapshot does not exist", not
  code); rerun passed: healthz ok, unsigned 401, non-root uid 999, lease_cycle 5 passed incl. new
  `job_leases_over_http` (helper PeerId shown when fresh, absent without registration, 404 for other device / the
  helper / unknown / malformed id, 400 for a body, 401 unsigned and forged signature, expired lease excluded after
  61 s, completed lease excluded). No leftover containers, volumes or images.
- **Not done / open:** staleness past 600 s is not exercised over HTTP (would need a 10-minute wait or a DB
  shortcut); covered by the shared `fresh_since` predicate and the "never registered" case. Core-agent half:
  requester polls this endpoint and calls `PeerNet::grant`. No coordinator-wide rate limiting yet.

## 2026-11-03 - core-agent (Claude): 1.L15 nc-agent runs an nc-net node; direct blob fetch with HTTP fallback

- **Branch/commits:** `feat/1.L15-agent-node` (this commit). Not merged.
- **Asked:** G1b: the agent starts an nc-net node, registers it with `POST /v1/devices/peer` and keeps that fresh;
  the requester serves a lease's blobs only to the helper named for that lease; the helper fetches from
  `LeaseResponse.peer`, checks the authenticated PeerId, verifies like the HTTP path, falls back to HTTP; budget is
  charged per chunk.
- **Done:**
  - `core/crates/nc-agent/src/peer.rs` (new): `PeerNet` (nc-net node with a fresh Ed25519 key per process, its own
    2-thread tokio runtime, in-memory lease-scoped trust set), `/nc/blob/1.0.0` chunk server (`grant`/`revoke`:
    serves only granted blobs to the granted PeerId, optional requester-side budget hook), helper `prepare`/`release`
    (dial hinted addrs with `/p2p/<hinted id>` so the handshake rejects another key; trust only for the lease),
    `fetch` (direct, 256 KiB chunks, each authorised for chunk + 256 B overhead before the request, Stop polled every
    20 ms, size + sha256 check as on HTTP, `.direct.part` always deleted; network/peer/verify failure -> HTTP;
    Stop/window/budget refusal -> no fallback), `register_request` (binding signature over
    `nc.v1.PeerBinding␀ || device key`, addrs without /p2p or unspecified IPs), `refresh_if_due` (every 240 s,
    retry 30 s, charged as Control traffic; 401/403/404 stop refreshing), `PathStats` (direct_in, http_in, served,
    fallbacks).
  - `coord.rs`: `Coordinator::register_peer` (default 404 unsupported), signed `HttpCoordinator` call, SkipRegister
    forwards. `session.rs`: `Backend.peer: Option<AgentPeer>`; module and inputs go through `peer::fetch`; the
    registration refresh runs from the main loop and the lease-renew loop. `config.rs`: starts an outbound-only node
    (no listener) and wires it in; start failure only logs and keeps HTTP. Tests' Backend literals get `peer: None`.
  - Cargo: nc-agent depends on nc-net, tokio (rt-multi-thread, time, sync, macros), futures. No nc-net API change.
- **Decisions:** (1) Per-process libp2p key (never on disk); the server binding is refreshed on start. (2) Hinted
  requester is trusted only in a separate in-memory TrustStore, only while that lease downloads (not pairing trust).
  (3) Production node listens on nothing: no firewall prompt and no wider bind (rule 7); the requester role needs a
  listen-address config field, which would break the App-owned `nc-bridge` AgentConfig literal, so it is not added.
  (4) The requester cannot learn its helper's PeerId: nothing in proto/ tells it (relay tokens are HMAC, not
  verifiable by devices). So `grant` exists and is tested but nothing in production calls it; helpers therefore fall
  back to HTTP today. Serving to unknown peers would break "only the peer named for that lease", so it was not done.
  (5) `/nc/blob/1.0.0` framing is defined in peer.rs, not proto/ (task said not to touch proto/); requested below.
- **Verified (real results, Windows, this worktree):** `cargo fmt --check` ok; `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D
  warnings` ok; `cargo test -j 2` in core/: every suite ok, 0 failed (nc-agent lib 48 passed incl. 7 new peer tests:
  direct fetch between two in-process nodes with 0 HTTP gets, budget spent = size + 3 x 256 B for 3 chunks and a
  cellular switch refused before any byte was served, wrong PeerId refused then HTTP, ungranted blob/peer refused,
  tampered chunk refused then HTTP with no part file left, no hint -> HTTP, registration binding verifies and refresh
  stops after 401).
- **Not done / open:** `infra/fleet-e2e.ps1` not run (C: had 7.5 GB free; the run builds Docker images); its X1
  check will now say UNEXPECTED-PASS because nc-agent links nc-net. No session-level test with a hinted lease
  (only the fetch path is tested). Requester grants need a proto source of the helper PeerId (request). Requester
  serve budget hook is not wired to the BudgetGate. Direct/HTTP byte counters are not shown to the owner yet (1.L16).
  Relay fallback is 1.L16.

## 2026-11-03 - Codex - feat/codex-linux-sandbox - 1.L8-1.L10



- **Asked:** implement the fail-closed Linux OS sandbox for nc-exec, test it on a real Linux kernel, preserve Windows, push a review branch, and remove the isolated worktree/build artifacts afterwards.

- **Done:** added namespaces, tmpfs pivot_root with only /worker, /lib and private read-only /proc, empty environment, descriptor/capability removal, no_new_privs, rlimits and a ready/resume gate. Added seccompiler allow-lists for x86_64/aarch64 and cgroup v2 memory/no-swap, pids and CPU limits. Cgroup attachment happens in pre_exec before loader startup. Added kernel events/peak usage, full-tree kill, Drop/teardown, owner-start-time-aware sweep and private staging cleanup. Kept the Windows method signatures and macOS refusal backend. Added Linux escape/lifecycle tests and an Ubuntu CI sandbox step. The executor also drains final OS limit events after process exit.

- **Decisions:** seccompiler 0.5.0 is Apache-2.0 OR BSD-3-Clause, already permitted by deny.toml; no policy exception was added. A trusted worker bootstrap applies all layers before job IPC/resume; a private descriptor-3 stream gates startup. clone3 returns ENOSYS to force the argument-checked pthread clone path. Native forks are killed on their first attempt; independent thread exhaustion verifies pids.max. The branch started at latest-fetched origin/main, 3ed7fe2.

- **Verified:** Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS x86_64 on WSL2 kernel 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2, ordinary user. All seven namespace flags together returned exit 0. A delegated systemd user scope accepted cpu/memory/pids controllers, all limits, cgroup.kill and removal. No Docker sandbox/security-opt flags were used because testing was directly on WSL2.

- **Verified:** core workspace fmt, clippy --all-targets with warnings denied, cargo test, and cargo deny check passed on Windows and Linux; builds/checks used -j 2. Windows nc-exec sandbox: 12 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored (cold-launch measurement). Linux real sandbox: 10 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored. SIGSYS/ProcessLimit covered socket, execve, ptrace, unshare, mount and fork; native OOM reported MemoryLimit with a 67108864-byte peak; pids exhaustion reported ProcessLimit. Kill with a grandchild present took 5.575011 ms; full Stop returned in 7.107031 ms. Kernel state, empty environment/fds, rlimits, filesystem denial, suspended start, teardown, Drop, stale/live-owner sweep and staging removal passed. Test-only refusal hooks exercised unavailable user namespaces/cgroups. ARM64 cargo check and clippy --all-targets passed with a real ARM64 GCC; the compiler also produced ELF e_machine=183. The CI-style User=1000 delegated transient-service flow also passed 10/10 locally (kill 6.237284 ms, Stop 13.69857 ms), without requiring a login bus.

- **Failures fixed:** an initial moved-gate compile error and one SAFETY-comment placement warning; the expanded real suite initially passed 8/10 and identified a missing Rust statx metadata syscall and tempfile's non-private default directory mode. Raw-argument strace confirmed statx. The allow-list now includes that ordinary metadata operation, staging explicitly uses 0700, and the final untraced suite passed 10/10. No isolation layer was disabled.

- **Security invariants:** 3 (all layers required before job IPC), 4 (kill/reap/remove on teardown/Drop and stale sweep), 5 (measured Stop/kill below 1 s), 10 (OS-only diagnostic redaction, no job data/path logging), 11 (documented unsafe confined to nc-exec; clippy and deny passed).

- **Not done / limits:** no native ARM64 execution or older-kernel memory.current fallback run; GitHub-hosted CI execution is not claimed by these local results. Existing external-fleet/Docker-dependent ignored tests were not enabled. Full commands, output excerpts and implementation choices are in core/crates/nc-exec/LINUX-SANDBOX.md.

- **Temporary resources:** C:\nc-target-codex became a junction to D:\nc-target-codex when C: ran short of space; WSL artifacts used its linux subdirectory. Subsequent builds disabled debug info/incremental caches using environment variables only. Rust/GCC/cargo-deny/strace tools were extracted there, with no Linux system packages installed. No containers/images were created and no Docker prune command was run. Post-push worktree/build cleanup is reported in the final hand-back.

- **Commits:** this commit (on top of 56755f8).


- **Asked:** fix CI 41346901474 (`real_job_cycle_over_http` got one 500 during the 20-call two-device lease


  race), re-review the branch for invariants 7/8/10 and blob GET scoping.

  that the task has no live lease, no result from this device, and is still queued/leased; a lost race


  rolls back and tries the next task (ends as 404 "no work"). New migration `0003_one_active_lease.sql`


  adds a unique partial index (one active lease per task, all devices). `From<sqlx::Error>` now logs


  SQLSTATE and constraint name only (no driver message, which can echo row values).


- **Decisions:** root cause: `FOR UPDATE ... SKIP LOCKED` in READ COMMITTED re-evaluates only the locked


  task row once the competing transaction commits; the `NOT EXISTS(leases ...)` subquery still used the


  old snapshot, so a second caller could lease the same task. Same device: violated `one_live_device_task`


  (the 500); different devices: would have silently double-leased. Unique-violation is not mapped to 404;


  with the re-check it should not occur, and if it does it stays a logged 500 (not swallowed).

  returns duplicate, different result 409); blob GET requires requester, or live lease on the job, or


  committed result for the requester; signed-request auth on all routes; single error format; no new logs


  of manifests/blobs/signatures/tokens found. No further defects fixed.

- **Asked:** find out why Windows Mobile Hotspot was on, with a helper connected, but the Wi-Fi Direct tab still showed


  "Mode: A | Stopped, Interface: -, IP: -".


- **Done:** `wifidirect._read_adapter_rows`: `Get-NetIPConfiguration` threw for a hidden adapter that has no IP interface


  (here ifIndex 17). `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` did not catch the error raised inside the module under


  `$ErrorActionPreference='Stop'`, so the whole PowerShell query exited 1 and the app saw **no adapters at all**. It


  then never detected the hotspot and fell back to starting its own Wi-Fi Direct publisher. That call is now wrapped in


  `try { ... } catch { $null }` for each adapter.


- **Decisions:** one-line fix. The command is still constant (nothing interpolated). Security invariants unchanged.


- **Verified:** before the fix the query returned rc 1 and `direct_interfaces()` returned `[]`. After it,


  `direct_interfaces()` returns the "Microsoft Wi-Fi Direct Virtual Adapter #4" at 192.168.137.1/24, owner=True,


  peer 192.168.137.158. `.venv` pytest `-k "direct or wifi or link or discovery"`: 89 passed.


- **Also:** `link_gui.firewall_status` always said "Firewall rule needs updating" because Windows reports the rule's


  remote address as `192.168.137.0/255.255.255.0` and the code string-compared it to `192.168.137.0/24`. It now


  compares parsed networks. With the real rule: "Direct-link rule enabled for this address and subnet."


  `-k "firewall or link_gui or direct"`: 44 passed. App relaunched (owner approved); controller listens on 192.168.137.1:8765.


- **Also:** owner reported PowerShell windows popping up. Under pythonw every console child opens a window unless


  started with CREATE_NO_WINDOW; only `wifidirect._run` and the job runner did. Added it to the three PowerShell calls in


  `link_gui.py` (firewall status runs on every Wi-Fi Direct refresh), `security.protect_path` (icacls) and the two


  icacls calls in `sandbox.py` (Windows-only flag, 0 elsewhere). `-k "firewall or link or direct or sandbox or


  security"`: 115 passed. Not yet seen in the relaunched GUI. Same flag added to `updater._run` (git/pip).


- **Also (GUI slowness):** owner said the interface is very slow and asked about another UI technology. Measured: the


  adapter query took 12.3 s per call and the firewall check 4.0 s, both started on every 5 s Wi-Fi Direct refresh.


  Tkinter itself was not the cause (work already runs on background threads). Rewrote the adapter query as one bulk


  call per cmdlet joined by ifIndex, without `Get-NetIPConfiguration` (gateway from `Get-NetRoute 0.0.0.0/0`): 2.6-2.9 s,


  same detected interface and peer. The firewall check now reruns only when the address changes, once a minute, or


  after "Allow through firewall". `-k "firewall or link or direct or wifi or discovery or config"`: 90 passed.


  Recommended keeping Tkinter. Not yet seen in the GUI.


- **Also (controller would not start):** popup "Port 8765 is used by another program (PID …, pythonw.exe)" where the


  PID was the app itself. Cause: `controller.json` `bind_hosts` held 192.168.137.1, and the hotspot had turned off


  (Windows hotspot power saving), so that bind failed after 10.63.182.8 and 127.0.0.1 had bound; `port_in_use_message`


  then found the app's own listener. Fixes in `controller.py`: `start()` skips an extra saved address this PC no longer


  has (logged, kept in config); main address and loopback still must bind. `port_in_use_message` ignores this


  process's own listeners and says when the address is missing. Two tests added in `tests/test_local_connection.py`;


  that file plus `test_controller.py`: 13 passed. App restarted at the owner's request.

  `save_config` of the in-memory cfg); not investigated.

  - `core/crates/nc-agent/src/jobs.rs` (new): `JobStore` under `<data_dir>/requests/<uuid>/`. `stage` writes `record.json` (signed manifest, blob hashes, phase) and copies of the blobs before anything is sent. `ensure_submitted` re-checks each staged blob's hash, uploads, submits (the coordinator accepts the same signed manifest again, so a crash anywhere is idempotent), marks `submitted` and deletes the staged copies. `status`/`wait`/`fetch` submit first if still staged. ## 2026-11-03 - Claude (Core agent) - `feat/1.L12-win-service` - task 1.L12 (gap G7a)











- Asked: run nc-agent as a Windows service (install/uninstall/start/stop, clean Stop within 1 s, least-privilege account, ProgramData data dir with tight ACLs, restart on failure, file logs), and test it for real on this PC.





- Done:





  - `core/crates/nc-agent/src/service.rs` (new, Windows only): `nc-agent service install --config <p> | uninstall | start | stop`, and the SCM entry `service run --config <p>`. Account `NT SERVICE\nc-agent` (virtual account, not LocalSystem), auto start. Restart on failure after 5 s, then 30 s, then nothing; the counter resets after 1 day; non-crash failures (service-specific exit code 1) also count. Install refuses a data_dir that is not under `%ProgramData%`. It then cuts ACL inheritance and grants only SYSTEM (F), Administrators (F) and the service account (M) via `icacls`, and gives the service read access to the config file if it lives outside the data dir. If `NC_ENROLL_SECRET` is set at install, it goes into `<data_dir>\enroll.secret` (never printed). SCM Stop/Shutdown sends the existing authenticated loopback `Shutdown` control command, so the stop path is the same as a console daemon exit (session stop, job cancel, lease failed `STOP`, sandbox teardown). A Stop that arrives before start-up finishes is queued and sent once the control port is up. Service logs go to `<data_dir>\logs\nc-agent.log` (same tracing events as the console, no ANSI).





  - `core/crates/nc-agent/src/main.rs`: subcommand parsing; `run_daemon` takes an on-ready hook. Console `run --config` is unchanged.





  - `core/crates/nc-agent/src/config.rs`: the enrolment secret comes from `NC_ENROLL_SECRET`, else from `enroll.secret` in the data dir.





  - `core/crates/nc-agent/Cargo.toml`: `windows-service = "0.8"` (MIT OR Apache-2.0), Windows target only.





- Decisions (Core agent): a virtual account, because nothing in the sandbox needs LocalSystem. AppContainer profiles and Job Objects are created by the calling user; whether this works from a virtual-account service session is **not yet verified** (see below). Uninstall keeps the data dir (device key) on purpose. Control port behaviour is unchanged (loopback bind + token); the token file is now admin/service-only, so `nc status` against the service must run elevated.





- Verified (core/, CARGO_TARGET_DIR=C:\nc-target, -j 2, low priority): `cargo fmt --check` clean; `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean (the `define_windows_service!` macro did not trip `unsafe_code = deny`); `cargo test` 42 binaries, 309 passed, 0 failed, 6 ignored (new: args parse cases, data-dir-under-ProgramData check, SCM status codes); `cargo deny check licenses` ok.





- Not done / open: **no real service install was run.** The session was not elevated (`whoami /groups`: Medium Mandatory Level), and `sc query nc-agent` gave 1060 (not installed). So the following are all unverified: SCM start/stop timings, Stop within 1 s from the service, AppContainer + Job Object under `NT SERVICE\nc-agent`, restart on failure, and the ACLs as applied. The owner must run the elevated test given in the 1.L12 hand-back. No Event Log source (file log only).

  - `core/crates/nc-agent/src/jobs.rs` (new): `JobStore` under `<data_dir>/requests/<uuid>/`. `stage` writes `record.json` (signed manifest, blob hashes, phase) and copies of the blobs before anything is sent. `ensure_submitted` re-checks each staged blob's hash, uploads, submits (the coordinator accepts the same signed manifest again, so a crash anywhere is idempotent), marks `submitted` and deletes the staged copies. `status`/`wait`/`fetch` submit first if still staged. Transient errors (network, 5xx, 429) retried with backoff until the timeout, as in 1.L1; others end at once. The committed output hash/size is pinned in the record the first time it is seen; a later different committed output is refused (`OutputChanged`). Downloads are checked against the committed hash (`requester::fetch_output`). Output files are written via temp file + rename. Ids must parse as UUIDs (no path traversal).

## 2026-11-03 - Claude (Core agent) - `feat/1.L12-win-service` - task 1.L12 (gap G7a)











- Asked: run nc-agent as a Windows service (install/uninstall/start/stop, clean Stop within 1 s, least-privilege account, ProgramData data dir with tight ACLs, restart on failure, file logs), and test it for real on this PC.





- Done:





  - `core/crates/nc-agent/src/service.rs` (new, Windows only): `nc-agent service install --config <p> | uninstall | start | stop`, and the SCM entry `service run --config <p>`. Account `NT SERVICE\nc-agent` (virtual account, not LocalSystem), auto start. Restart on failure after 5 s, then 30 s, then nothing; the counter resets after 1 day; non-crash failures (service-specific exit code 1) also count. Install refuses a data_dir that is not under `%ProgramData%`. It then cuts ACL inheritance and grants only SYSTEM (F), Administrators (F) and the service account (M) via `icacls`, and gives the service read access to the config file if it lives outside the data dir. If `NC_ENROLL_SECRET` is set at install, it goes into `<data_dir>\enroll.secret` (never printed). SCM Stop/Shutdown sends the existing authenticated loopback `Shutdown` control command, so the stop path is the same as a console daemon exit (session stop, job cancel, lease failed `STOP`, sandbox teardown). A Stop that arrives before start-up finishes is queued and sent once the control port is up. Service logs go to `<data_dir>\logs\nc-agent.log` (same tracing events as the console, no ANSI).





  - `core/crates/nc-agent/src/main.rs`: subcommand parsing; `run_daemon` takes an on-ready hook. Console `run --config` is unchanged.





  - `core/crates/nc-agent/src/config.rs`: the enrolment secret comes from `NC_ENROLL_SECRET`, else from `enroll.secret` in the data dir.





  - `core/crates/nc-agent/Cargo.toml`: `windows-service = "0.8"` (MIT OR Apache-2.0), Windows target only.





- Decisions (Core agent): a virtual account, because nothing in the sandbox needs LocalSystem. AppContainer profiles and Job Objects are created by the calling user; whether this works from a virtual-account service session is **not yet verified** (see below). Uninstall keeps the data dir (device key) on purpose. - **Asked:** G5 server side: resumable chunked uploads into the coordinator blob store, per-chunk and final hash






  checks, existing caps and auth, GC of abandoned partials, keep the single PUT, write the exact HTTP contract for






  1.L6.






- **Done:**






  - New `server/crates/nc-coordinator/src/resumable.rs`: `GET /v1/blobs/{sha}/upload/{size}` (held offset in






    `x-nc-upload-offset`) and `PUT /v1/blobs/{sha}/upload/{size}/{offset}` (one chunk, 1 B to 4 MiB, signed






    NC-REQ-V1 with the chunk hash sent in `x-nc-chunk-sha256`, signature checked before the body is read). Session =






    (device, sha, size) in one append-only partial file; exact-offset append + fsync, rolled back on a failed






    write; 409 `upload_offset` reports where to resume; 409 `upload_busy` for a concurrent request; at most 8 open






    sessions per device; last chunk checks the whole file and publishes it. Any failure there deletes the session.






  - `blobs.rs`: publication split out into `publish()`, which the single PUT and the last chunk share (same






    advisory lock, `blobs`/`blob_uploaders` rows). The single PUT is unchanged.






  - GC: `resumable::gc` deletes partials (and single-PUT temporaries left by a killed process) not written for






    24 h, skipping sessions in flight; `main.rs` runs it at start-up and hourly (tokio `time` feature added).

    G5 marked server-done.

    test `resumable_upload_over_http` (9 MiB blob in 3 chunks with a simulated interruption and resume, 413 for an






    oversize chunk, 401 for a bad signature, 400 for a chunk hash mismatch and for a final hash mismatch that






    discards the session, 409 offset replay, another device cannot see or extend the session, module/input






    uploaded by chunks make the requester an uploader so the GET returns 200 with the exact bytes).
